question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), what is the ratio for a single-age group of infants (birth up to 12 months)? Answer as the number of children per teaching personnel.
quote: Child Care Centers, Drop-In Programs, and Part-Day Programs Single-Age Group Chart ... Ratios Maximum Group Size Infants 1:4 8
section: OAC 340:110-3-286(a); OAC 340 Appendix GG (Single-Age Group Chart)
notes: Maximum group 8. Only teaching personnel count in ratios. Mixed-age groups use the Mixed-Age Group Chart (e.g., infants and older 1:8 with no more than two children under 2 per teaching personnel). Swimming/wading ratio for infants is 1:1.

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), what is the ratio for a single-age group of 3-year-olds? Answer as the number of children per teaching personnel.
quote: Child Care Centers, Drop-In Programs, and Part-Day Programs Single-Age Group Chart ... 3-year-olds 1:12 24
section: OAC 340:110-3-286(a); OAC 340 Appendix GG (Single-Age Group Chart)
notes: Maximum group 24. A mixed-age group of 3-year-olds and older is 1:15 with no more than six 3-year-olds per teaching personnel. Out-of-school time programs: 3-year-olds 1:12 (group 24).

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), what is the ratio for a single-age group of 4-year-olds? Answer as the number of children per teaching personnel.
quote: Child Care Centers, Drop-In Programs, and Part-Day Programs Single-Age Group Chart ... 4-year-olds 5-year-olds (and older single-age groups) 1:15 30 1:20 40
section: OAC 340:110-3-286(a); OAC 340 Appendix GG (Single-Age Group Chart)
notes: Maximum group 30. A mixed-age group of 4-year-olds and older is 1:18 (group 36) with no more than eight 4-year-olds per teaching personnel.

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), what is the ratio for a single-age group of 5-year-olds and older (the chart's oldest band, which covers school-age children)? Answer as the number of children per teaching personnel.
quote: Child Care Centers, Drop-In Programs, and Part-Day Programs Single-Age Group Chart ... 4-year-olds 5-year-olds (and older single-age groups) 1:15 30 1:20 40
section: OAC 340:110-3-286(a); OAC 340 Appendix GG (Single-Age Group Chart)
notes: Maximum group 40. Other program types differ: out-of-school time programs 5 and older 1:20 with no set maximum group; day camps 1:15; swimming ratio for age 6 and older 1:10.

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), what is the maximum group size for a single-age group of 4-year-olds?
quote: Child Care Centers, Drop-In Programs, and Part-Day Programs Single-Age Group Chart ... 4-year-olds 5-year-olds (and older single-age groups) 1:15 30 1:20 40
section: OAC 340:110-3-286(b); OAC 340 Appendix GG (Single-Age Group Chart)
notes: Maximum group size does not apply when groups are combined for special activities, outdoor play, meals, snacks, rest time and field trips (286(b)(2)); ratios still apply.

question: What is the minimum age for a teacher (the teaching personnel position with primary responsibility for the direct care of children) at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3)?
quote: Teachers. The program employs individuals or utilizes volunteers meeting the position specific requirements in (1) through (3) of this subsection. (1) Position specific qualifications. Teachers: (A) are at least 18 years of age;
notes: Only teaching personnel count in ratios (286(a)), and teaching personnel include assistant teachers, who may be 16 (284.2(d)(1)(A)) but may not have sole responsibility for a group for more than three hours a day. Master teachers must also be 18.

question: What minimum level of the Oklahoma Director's Credential must the director of an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) hold?
answer: A current Bronze (or higher) level certificate
quote: The director: (A) is at least 21 years of age; (B) has satisfactory work experience; (C) has a current bronze or higher level certificate per OAC 340 Appendix EE Oklahoma Director's Credential;
notes: The director must also be at least 21. Appendix EE sets the education, experience and annual renewal hours for each credential level.

question: Teaching personnel at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) must maintain a current Oklahoma Professional Development Ladder (OPDL) certificate. How many clock-hours of training per year does renewal of a Level 1 OPDL certificate require?
quote: APPENDIX FF. OKLAHOMA PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT LADDER ... Annual Renewal Clock Hours ... 1 12 clock hours of ECE/CD/SA training3 in the past 12 months 12 hours3
notes: Level 1 is the lowest level; Levels 2 through 11 require 20 annual renewal clock-hours, and required master teachers need Level 4 or higher. No more than 6 informal hours count. Directors renew hours under the Director's Credential (Appendix EE).

question: What is the minimum indoor floor space per child required at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3)?
quote: Square footage for licensed capacity. A minimum amount of indoor play area is required. (A) There is at least 35 square feet of floor space per child for routine use by children.
notes: Rooms used only by infants need 40 sq ft per infant for new construction, space not previously licensed, or programs licensed after November 1, 2016 (301(b)(1)(B)). Restrooms, kitchens, hallways, offices and similar areas are excluded.

question: For an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) with a licensed capacity of 23 or fewer children, what is the minimum outdoor play area per child, calculated on the licensed capacity?
unit: square feet per child of licensed capacity
quote: When the licensed capacity is 23 or fewer children there is at least 75 square feet of outdoor play area per child for the licensed capacity.
notes: Counted per child of licensed capacity. Capacity 24 or more: 75 sq ft per child for at least one-third of the licensed capacity or 1,800 sq ft, whichever is greater (301(c)(1)(B)); with less than 75 sq ft per child for full capacity a rotation schedule is used.

question: What is the maximum temperature of the running water at hand washing sinks in an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3)?
quote: Hand washing facilities have: (A) operable sinks with running water between 80 and 120 degrees Fahrenheit;
notes: The rule sets a range of 80 to 120°F.

question: What must an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) obtain before administering a medication to a child?
answer: Signed parent permission for that medication, obtained before administration on an OKDHS or program form
quote: Medication permission. Signed parent permission for each medication is obtained, prior to administration, on an OKDHS or program form containing the same information.
notes: Parent instructions must match the container or a physician's written statement. For chronic conditions permission may be for 12 months or less. Medication must be in the original container labeled with the child's full name (295(f)).

question: How often must an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) conduct fire drills?
quote: per required scheduling. (i) Monthly. Monthly drills include: (I) fire drills conducted by evacuating and meeting at pre-determined locations;
notes: Tornado drills are also monthly. Drills are held at varied times so children and personnel take part in each type at least once every three months (279(g)(1)(A)).

question: How long must an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) keep children's daily attendance records?
quote: Children's attendance. Daily attendance is: (i) promptly documented on paper, including the child's full name and arrival and departure time; and (ii) maintained, on paper or electronically, for at least 12 months.
notes: Personnel records: at least 12 months after the last date of employment (281.3(b)).

question: In what position must infants be placed for sleeping at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3)?
answer: On their back, unless a documented medical reason says otherwise
quote: Infants are placed on their back for sleeping, unless there is a medical reason an infant should not sleep in this position as documented per OAC 340:110-3-281.4(b).
notes: Infants able to turn over are placed on their back initially but may then sleep in the position they prefer.

question: By when must an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) notify Licensing of a child injury requiring emergency medical attention?
answer: By the next OKDHS business day
quote: The owner, responsible entity, or director notifies Licensing by the next Oklahoma Human Services (OKDHS) business day of: ... (N) a child injury requiring emergency medical attention;
notes: Deadline is to the licensing agency. Parents must be notified immediately of an injury that may need evaluation by a licensed physician (280(d)(1)(E)).

question: By when must an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) obtain a child's immunization record or exemption?
answer: Before the child's first day of attendance
quote: Immunization records. An immunization record or exemption is obtained prior to the first day of attendance and is updated when the child receives additional vaccines.

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), how many personnel with current CPR and first aid certification must be present with children at all times (on-site in each building where children are, off-site, and in each vehicle)?
quote: At all times, at least one personnel with current CPR and first aid certification is present with children: (i) on-site, including in each building where children are present; (ii) off-site; and (iii) in each vehicle during transportation.
notes: The director, master teachers, teachers and assistant teachers must each obtain CPR and first aid certification within three months (284.1(b)(3)(B); 284.2).

question: Does an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3) have to keep a specific minimum distance between cribs, cots, or mats, and if not, what spacing standard applies?
answer: No fixed distance for child care centers; rest equipment must be spaced to give teaching personnel easy access to children and allow safe evacuation
quote: Spacing. Equipment is spaced to allow easy access to children by the teaching personnel and for the safe evacuation of children.
notes: No numeric distance is set for child care centers. A three-foot spacing applies only to programs for sick children (OAC 340:110-3-311(i)(4)).

question: Under the Oklahoma Child Care Facilities Licensing Act, as reprinted in OKDHS Publication 14-05, how long does a child care center license remain in force?
answer: Until it is revoked; licenses have no fixed expiration
quote: All licenses shall be in force unless revoked as authorized by Section 407 of this title.
notes: OAC 340:110-3-276(d)(3): authorization to operate is maintained based on compliance. Fire and health inspections are required at least every two years, and authorization lapses after 12 consecutive months with no care provided (276(d)(6)).

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), a mixed-age group of 3-year-olds and older has a ratio of 1:15. What is the maximum number of 3-year-olds allowed per teaching personnel in that group?
quote: Mixed-Age Group Chart ... 3-year-olds and older 1:15 No more than six 3-year-olds per teaching personnel 30
notes: Maximum group 30. If a mixed-age group is understaffed or over size under this chart, the Mixed-Age Group Exception lets the program apply the Single-Age chart using the youngest child's age.

question: During rest time at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), when one group of 3- through 5-year-olds is resting quietly or sleeping, how many teaching personnel at minimum must be present in the classroom (other teaching personnel required for ratio staying in the building)?
quote: Rest time – 3- through 5-year-olds. When children are resting quietly or sleeping, the exceptions in (i) and (ii) of this subparagraph may apply. (i) One group. At least one teaching personnel is present in the classroom. Other teaching personnel required for ratios remain in the building on the same floor.
notes: Ratios still apply; the other required staff must be in the building on the same floor. When groups are combined for rest, one teaching personnel per group must be in the room. The exception does not cover infants, 1- or 2-year-olds.

question: For an Oklahoma child care program licensed after November 1, 2016 (or new construction or space not previously licensed), how many square feet of floor space per infant are required in rooms occupied only by infants?
quote: However, new construction, existing space not previously licensed for child care, or programs licensed after November 1, 2016, are required to have 40 square feet of floor space per infant in rooms occupied only by infants.
notes: Other rooms: 35 sq ft per child (301(b)(1)(A)).

question: What is the minimum age for an assistant teacher at an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3)? (Assistant teachers are teaching personnel and can count in ratios.)
quote: Assistant teachers. The program may employ individuals or utilize volunteers meeting the position specific requirements in (1) through (4) of this subsection. (1) Position specific qualifications. Assistant teachers: (A) are at least 16 years of age;
notes: Assistant teachers must be overseen by an on-site director, master teacher, or teacher (each overseeing no more than two), and may not have sole responsibility for a group for more than three hours a day or during higher risk activities.

question: At an Oklahoma licensed child care center (OKDHS Licensing Requirements for Child Care Programs, OAC 340:110-3), one master teacher is required for every how many children of licensed capacity?
quote: Required master teachers. At least one master teacher is required for every 60 children of the licensed capacity.
notes: Required master teachers need an OPDL certificate of Level 4 or higher; a one-year probationary period is available when replacing a master teacher.
